text:
samir: FYI BrightCart reported degraded latency and 5xxs on their Dedicated pool starting ~09:10 UTC. They say traffic is steady but their tenant is oscillating between 3 and 6 instances every ~6m.
kelly: ugh, sounds like the autoscaler is hunting. any quick telemetry?
samir: attaching a small excerpt from their events stream below (filtered):
```
2026-03-16T09:09:58Z autoscale decision: scale_up target=4 reason=cpu=78% cooldown=300s
2026-03-16T09:14:12Z autoscale decision: scale_down target=3 reason=cpu=30% cooldown=30s
2026-03-16T09:20:05Z autoscale decision: scale_up target=5 reason=queue_latency=420ms cooldown=300s
2026-03-16T09:26:09Z autoscale decision: scale_down target=3 reason=cpu=28% cooldown=30s
2026-03-16T09:32:11Z autoscale decision: scale_up target=6 reason=oom_evictions=1 cooldown=300s
```
samir: looks like very short effective cooldowns between downs and ups. probe windows also show bursty 95p token generation latencies.
eng_oncall: pinging autoscale-bot to show recent metric windows and policy for BrightCart (tenant id: bc-728). @autoscale-bot any context? :eyes:
autoscale-bot: policy(bc-728): min_replicas=2 max_replicas=10 target_cpu=60 target_queue_ms=300 scale_up_cooldown=300s scale_down_cooldown=60s down_policy=conservative
jorge: scale_down_cooldown=60s is pretty short given they have long-tail request patterns. We usually bias down cooldowns for batchy workloads to 5-10m.
maria: customer says they have async batch jobs that spike KV cache misses for a few minutes then quiet. Combined with prefix cache churn that could cause noisy neighbour pressure on same GPU nodes.
kelly: any noisy neighbor evidence (OOMs, eviction counts, container throttling)?
samir: from node logs: 
```
[09:31:57] node-12: gpu_mem_pressure=0.82, pod=bc-728-srv-5 oom_kill=1
[09:31:58] pod=bc-728-srv-5 restart_count=1
[09:31:59] node-12: preemption=false, throttled=true
```
eng_oncall: okay. This looks like local resource contention caused a pod restart which triggered immediate scale reactions. The controller then scaled down too quickly and we fell back into contention.
jorge: reproducer idea: run a synthetic workload that simulates long-generation KV miss + 10 concurrent requests for 3m windows. Use vegeta or a simple loop: 
```
for i in {1..10}; do curl -s -X POST "https://dedicated.brightcart.prod/generate" -d '@prompt.json' & done; sleep 180
```
maria: also check batching stats (in console -> pools -> bc-728 -> metrics) for token_batch_size and queue_length. If batching spikes then latency SLOs will jump and autoscaler will interpret it as sustained load.
kelly: immediate mitigation options?
samir: proposed steps: 1) increase scale_down_cooldown for bc-728 to 600s (10m) 2) apply node isolation (pod anti-affinity) to spread replicas across nodes 3) pin a small reserve pool for their tenant for next 24h 4) ask BrightCart to throttle background job bursts if possible.
eng_oncall: I'll apply config change (1) and set anti-affinity (2) now, and spin up reserve [temporary]. Will monitor.
eng_oncall: done — scale_down_cooldown=600s applied at 09:48 UTC, anti-affinity injected. Monitoring for 45m. :white_check_mark:
samir: thanks. please collect controller decision traces (controller.log) for the window after change and any evictions.
eng_oncall: grabbing traces: `kubectl logs deployment/autoscaler -n infra --since=1h | grep bc-728 > /tmp/bc-trace.log`
jorge: long-term: we should add hysteresis to the decision function (require sustained window crossing for 2 samples instead of 1) and consider reactive guard against OOM-driven scale ups. I'll file a follow-up RFC.
maria: cc @product-observability — we need a dashboard tile showing eviction-driven scale ups by tenant.
kelly: BrightCart ops responded: "after your changes latency looks stable, saw one 503 during the restart window, thanks"
samir: mark as in-progress; we'll reconvene after monitoring window. If oscillation resumes we'll look at making default scale_down_cooldown larger for tenants with long-tail workloads. :thumbsup:
